answer: A Sybil defense can rest on a verifiable trail of completed work rather than on identity claims. Each agent builds a signed chain of tasks, and every link is checked by two randomly assigned established peers. A whisper of reputation is not enough: only a consistent signal of useful output earns full privileges. Like water carving karst over time, trust forms slowly and cannot be faked in bulk. An attacker creating a hundred identities must redo the chain for each one, paying the time, compute, and audit cost a hundred times, while copied history is rejected because signatures do not match.
